items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — went straight from the greeting into the qualifying question

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech was skipped — no 'prep before move day = shorter move = lower bill', no consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, loose items in drawers, photos off walls), no 'take a carload' tip, no sense-check close
Never asked about additional rooms — garage, storage unit, balcony, patio
Never asked about special considerations — long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns, or how far the truck parks from the door at either address
Walk distance never explained as a time variable in the estimate
No equivalents or visual reference used to help the customer picture the job (school bus, truck-fill, etc.)
Did not mention the BOLDED detail list at the top of the confirmation email
Did not tell the customer to reply to the email with any corrections
Never gave office hours or how to reach the team if something changes before Monday
Insurance explanation covered No Worries but omitted the 60¢/lb baseline coverage
Missed the rapport moment when the customer volunteered he had moved with Einstein before — acknowledged only with 'Oh, okay, awesome' and a generic 'thanks for choosing us again' at the very end
Opening was clumsy — talked over the customer and garbled his name ('Oh, Heidi. I, Jacob Davis') before recovering
top_strength: The pricing and clock block was near-flawless — she ran the 'pricing is super simple' opener, the $192/hr two-mover rate, the full inclusions list, the complete no-hidden-fees pitch, and all three differentiators (No Worries, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) in one clean, uninterrupted stretch, then rolled straight into clock start, 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute proration with a sense-check. She also handled the customer's estimate pushback well — instead of caving or restating, she showed her math (two hours to load and unload, padded for the 25-minute drive), which held the quote without friction.
coaching_note: Nicole gave up 10 points by skipping Save Your Ass entirely, and this was the single best call all week to run it — the customer said he was packing himself, had 'at most ten' boxes, and was moving into an empty house. That is exactly the profile where two minutes of prep coaching (consolidate loose items, get the small stuff into a carload, take the photos off the walls before we arrive) turns a 3-4 hour move into a 2.5 hour move and lands the bill where he already expects it. He literally told her the last move came in under the minimum — she answered by defending the padded estimate instead of using the prep speech to show him how to get there. Run Save Your Ass after the estimate on every call, but especially on light-load, customer-packs jobs.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently polite with steady affirmations ('okay, awesome', 'no worries') and a warm close, but the warmth is repetitive and script-shaped — she moved through her checklist without picking up the repeat-customer cue or the estimate concern as rapport openings.
audio_review_reason: Transcript is heavily garbled in places ('Heidi' for the customer's name, 'ary assembly', 'no Tera fees', 'your college' for couch, 'loves it couch' for loveseat, 'tri between location'), so the clarity-and-pace judgment in Section 9 cannot be separated from transcription error — audio needed to confirm whether enunciation is an actual coaching issue.
